subject: Postmortem: surge-induced 5xx/429, timeouts and retry storms
thread_text:
From: Elena Morales <elena.morales@saasco.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: SaaSCo Support <support@saasco.com>
Date: 2026-02-18 09:12 -0800
Subject: Elevated errors and timeouts impacting production

Marissa —

We started seeing a flood of 5xx and 429s in our production traffic starting around 02:00 UTC this morning. Customers reported timeouts and partial responses. Attached is a screenshot from our dashboard and two request IDs that failed: req_3a7b2f and req_3a7b9c. The failures are affecting our billing page and a set of background webhook deliveries. Can someone confirm root cause and ETA for a fix? This is impacting a handful of customers and our incident ops team is escalating.

Thanks,
Elena

SaaSCo — Sr. Ops Manager

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-02-18 10:08 -0800
Subject: Re: Elevated errors and timeouts impacting production

Triage summary (initial):
- Timeline: spike began 2026-02-18T02:05:00Z, peaked 02:14Z–02:28Z, subsided after 02:45Z when we added capacity.
- Symptoms: burst of short-lived requests with large seq lengths; queueing increased between frontend and model pool; autoscaler scaled slower than expected due to min-instance gating and a bug in the scale-down cooldown window.
- Root cause (preliminary): autoscaler cooldown bug + tight per-tenant token bucket + aggressive client retry logic -> queueing and backpressure -> 429s and eventually 5xx from overloaded model workers. Retry storms amplified the problem.
- Observed gaps: no high-sensitivity alert for 429-rate delta vs baseline; request-queue-length was not surfaced on the SaaSCo routing policy dashboard; the runbook pointed to adding capacity but did not include immediate throttling or client guidance.

Immediate mitigation enacted:
1) Bumped dedicated pool for SaaSCo by +40% (temporary).
2) Applied short-term route-level throttling to background webhook endpoints.
3) Rolled a small patch to autoscaler to avoid triggering scale-down during sustained short bursts.
4) Contacted SaaSCo ops with suggested client-side backoff (exponential with jitter) as a stop-gap.

Attachments: timeline.csv, heap_snapshot.log (snippet)

Next actions (we should capture in postmortem):
- Write a runbook step for "retry storms": include immediate throttling, client guidance, and patch suggestions. Owner: Dylan. Target: 2026-02-22.
- Add a high-sensitivity 429 delta alert and queue-length signal to per-tenant dashboards. Owner: Jonas. Target: 2026-02-24.
- Review autoscale cooldown defaults and add a per-tenant override for critical customers. Owner: Rachel. Target: 2026-03-01.
- SLO tuning: revisit P99 latency and error budgets for routes with background work vs user-facing endpoints. Owner: Marissa + Product. Target: 2026-03-05.

I'll draft a short postmortem and share the doc.

—Dylan
Dylan Brooks
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-02-19 16:20 -0800
Subject: Postmortem draft and owner list — please review

Team — I uploaded an initial postmortem draft to Confluence (link below) and collected the action items from Dylan. Key items and owners below; add comments in the doc if your ETA needs to move.

Final proposed action list: 
- Runbook: "Retry storms / 429 surge" with step-by-step mitigations (throttle, temp capacity, client guidance). Owner: Dylan. ETA: 2026-02-22.
- Alerting: 429 delta alert + queue-length per-tenant dashboard. Owner: Jonas. ETA: 2026-02-24.
- Autoscaler: patch permanent fix and per-tenant cooldown override. Owner: Rachel. ETA: 2026-03-01.
- SLOs: Re-evaluate P95/P99 for endpoints; introduce an error budget policy that triggers automatic protective throttling when budget is exhausted. Owner: Marissa + Product. ETA: 2026-03-05.
- Capacity planning: run stress test for SaaSCo workloads with representative seq length distribution; add capacity reserve for top-10 customers. Owner: Ops Infra. ETA: 2026-03-12.
- Customer communications & credits: Monica to coordinate customer outreach and propose credits based on lost transactions. ETA: 2026-02-21.

Please review the Confluence doc at: https://confluence.redwood.ai/space/OPS/pages/SaaSCo-Retry-Storm-Postmortem
PagerDuty incident: https://pagerduty.com/incidents/PD-981234

I'll publish the finalized postmortem once we have owner ETAs.

—Marissa
